newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy ends Middle East mission upbeat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy ends Middle East mission upbeat.

text.p: U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross said on Wednesday he was leaving the Middle East having begun to revive Israeli-Palestinian security cooperation following a suicide attack.

"I am concluding this trip with the belief that we have created a mechanism that begins to establish the security relationship," he told reporters after meeting Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat at the end of a four-day mission.

Ross said U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would "very clearly" be traveling to the region for the first time. He said he would be leaving on Wednesday night and report to the secretary of state who would then decide when to make the trip. Albright had conditioned her visit on progress in Israeli-Palestinian security coordination.

"The mission the president and the secretary sent me out on...was to affect the security relationship but also to prevent further deterioration, and I think that has happened at this point," said Ross, U.S. President Bill Clinton's special envoy.

He said he believed some of the measures which Israel had imposed on Palestinians following the suicide attack, particularly a closure on the West Bank and Gaza Strip, would be eased. But he did not say when.
Israel clamped a closure on the territories after the July 30 attack at a Jerusalem market claimed the lives of 16 people, including two suicide bombers. Z
